interest: This document illustrates the State Department's cross-referencing and indexing practices regarding Japanese economic activities in North America prior to World War II. It highlights regional Canadian sensitivities and growing public resentment in British Columbia over Japanese capital penetration into local natural resources during late 1937, amidst escalating Sino-Japanese conflict. It also shows how the U.S. Foreign Service closely monitored foreign investments in strategic raw materials across borders.
overview: This file contains a single State Department cross-reference sheet (Document File Note) dated December 1, 1937, filed under decimal number 894.503142 (Japanese capital investment in Canada). The sheet directs researchers to consular report 842.63/273 from Vancouver by Consul Davis, concerning public resentment manifested in British Columbia against increasing Japanese investments in the province's natural resources.

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing a consular report from Vancouver on public resentment in British Columbia against Japanese investments in provincial natural resources.
subfiles.summary: A Document File Note dated December 1, 1937, referencing a report from Consul Davis in Vancouver filed under 842.63/273. It notes growing resentment manifested in British Columbia against expanding Japanese capital investments in the province's natural resources. The note serves as an internal cross-reference linking the Japanese internal affairs files to the Canadian economic series.
subfiles.title: Document File Note regarding Japanese investments in British Columbia natural resources
